what: child_core_frame v5: lightweight the aft core frame of the AquaBeacon child unit by topology optimisation, keeping every functional interface of v4 (650 cm3).
units: mm / N / MPa (lengths mm, forces N, stresses MPa)

material.name: PETG
material.notes: Tough, good layer adhesion, low warp, water resistant. The default for AquaBeacon wet-side parts. Softer than PLA, so deflection governs more often than strength.

conditions.model: equivalent solid, high density, generous perimeters

printer.name: Bambu Lab X1-Carbon
printer.note: AMS-fed; the purge tower needs ~60x60 mm of plate on multi-material prints.

cases.name: L1 hoist 3g: lugs fixed, container + guard + gate weights down
L2s transport side hit 300 N (+X on back wall and lugs), container reacts
L2h transport landing on the hinge side (300 N +X through the knuckles), container reacts
L2r transport rear hit 300 N on the back wall (+Y), container reacts
L3 clamp preload: knob bolts pull the latch bosses and the gate pulls the knuckles (+Y), tube reacts on the bands
L5 landing 600 N up through the guard bosses, container reacts

design_freedom.note_fixed_points: 15 load/support footprint(s) sit on preserve at positions the CAD model chose. The optimiser decides how to reach them, not where they are.

the free region is only 2.0 voxels (6.00 mm) thick at its thinnest. Below about 3 voxels there is no room for a hole, so the topology there is set by the outline rather than chosen -- refine the grid or widen the design space.

the 5 support point(s) are fixed by preserve at lug_boss_R at [65.3, -10.9, 210.8]; lug_boss_L at [-65.1, -10.8, 210.8]; pocket_bot at [0.6, -37.8, -9.1]; pocket_top at [0.7, -38.7, 207.7]; band_mid at [0.6, -41.7, 100.0]. Where the part is held is an input to this study, not a result of it -- if the layout of the supports is itself meant to be optimised, that decision is currently being made in CAD.
